chapter: Learning from Fletcher's circle in New York
title: Bluies, Don Redman visiting, and learning from the heart not books
summary: Bad notes were called bluies; Redman sometimes joined the sessions. Hawkins explained chords simply by playing the notes, and Horace values this over books because soul cannot be bought.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: But getting back to Don -- Don made a few of these sessions. It got so interesting they'd talk about it on the bandstand. Don'd say, 'Why don't you guys invite me up some time?' Hawk said, 'Sure.' He'd come up and Don would bring his horn, and they'd talk, and of course Don knew all that stuff, and he would help out with these guys. And I've got some old records of Fletcher's, and this is why -- I think you didn't hear too many (unintelligible) blues.
What we call bluies. Bad notes. Those -- that's a musical term. They'd say, you made a bluie there, man.
A bluie. I'm not familiar with that. I know klinker and klunker.

That's right. Well, it means the same thing, but instead of -- I hit a bluie. Like Bex Stewart said, 'Man, I made a bluie but I sold it.' So these are the things that happened. But Hawk's house turned out to be a real institution.
: Was he able to talk in terms of chords, like he'd say this is E flat major, or would he say these are the notes that you just played, or --

He talked very simple to the guys during that time. In fact, he would take his horn and run the notes, which, you know, in those times -- well, those guys, they didn't want to be arrangers or anything. All they wanted to know what constituted that chord, what notes, and their memory was uncanny.
: They probably did it more from their own instrument, rather than thinking in terms of letter names of notes and things like that.
: They would just copy that sound.
-- that sound. It was a wonderful experience, and to me, that was greater than anything that you can pick up in books.

: Because I've often been told and finally later on it was the truth, you know, you go in the books, you can become mechanical, you know. A lot of like (Sounds), so much -- but if you played from your heart, the way you feel a thing, you give out -- that's when that soul comes in, and that's something you cannot buy, you know, in the books. You've got to know how to feel.
